newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Feed group passes on major corn tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Feed group passes on major corn tender.

text.p: Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group passed on a tender on Friday for two shipments of U.S. No.2 or Argentine corn, with each shipment ranging between 54,000 tonnes and 56,000 tonnes, due to the government's ban on pork export, traders said.
Earlier on Friday state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp cancelled a Friday's tender for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans.

Taiwan's cabinet-level Council of Agriculture on Thursday banned all exports of fresh and frozen pork temporarily due to an outbreak of the deadly and highly contagious foot and mouth disease in the island's hog population.
Japan's Agriculture Ministry on Friday banned Taiwan's pork imports indefinitely in the wake of the outbreak.
South Korea also announced a similar ban.
The council estimated that Taiwan exported six million out of the 14 million hogs it bred per year.

According to an industry survey, the hog industry's total production value stood at T$89 billion (US$3.24 billion) in 1994, comprising 20 percent of Taiwan's farm market and 60 percent of the livestock sector.
Taiwan's grain buyers estimated on Thursday that a disease-linked ban on pork exports would cause the island's imports of feed corn to fall by about one-fifth.
"Corn imports will drop significantly," one buyer said.

A survey of five major Taiwan grain importers found that all expected significant reductions in corn imports, with most estimating the downturn at about 1.2 million tonnes or 19 percent of the island's annual imports of 6.5 million tonnes.

Taiwan has been importing almost all of its corn from the United States, although recent high U.S. prices have prompted some importers to look to alterative sources in South America, particularly Argentina.
The feed group's main buyers are Taiwan's Formosa Oilseed, Fomau Cereal, Morn Sun Feed Mill and Shin Tai Industry.
Details for the passed tender are as follows:
U.S. Gulf Pacific N.W.
Tonnage Date/Location
Argentine ports
